communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, I hereby request the following records:

Please provide a copy of "Quote Q-465809" Referenced in Amendment 2 of Contract 3352.

On 6/23/26 the Pioneer Press published the following article:  https://www.twincities.com/2026/06/23/st-paul-police-docked-drones-responding-911-calls

This article states that SPPD acquired three docked drones for $350,000. It also states that SPPD has a total of 17-20 drones in total. To date, none of the documents that the city has provided reconcile to the information that SPPD provided to the Pioneer Press. We are asking that the city provides whatever documentation they have that substantiates the Pioneer Press article. We are asking for the paper trail that says the city has 17-20 drones, including the three docked drones for $350,000. The "Amendment 2" document that the city attorney's office provided to CM Kim's staff does not reconcile to what the Pioneer Press article states - it says 12 hardware licenses and compensation of $129,749.36 over five years. 

Please provide "Quote Q-465809" Referenced in Amendment 2 of Contract 3352, and/or any documentation substantiating the number of drones and cost reported to the Pioneer Press on 6/23/26.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

title: Tulsa Crime Data Open Records Request- NIBRS

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: Tulsa Crime Data Open Records Request- NIBRS
communications.communication:
Dear Open Records Coordinator,

I am writing on behalf of the Data Acquisition Lab to formally request access to public records under the Oklahoma Open Records Act, 51 § 24A.1 et seq. We are requesting anonymized incident-level violent crime information for data visualization and analysis, which will enable a more meaningful understanding of community-level trends. We plan to request this information on a quarterly basis going forward.

I am specifically requesting incident-level crime data from the Tulsa Police Department's UCR Part 1 and 2 offense records, from January 1st, 2019, to December 31, 2023. 

Please provide the following fields for each incident:
-Identifier: Case/Report Number
-Date/Time: Date of Offense & Time of Offense
-Offense Detail: Offense Code, Offense Description, Offense Category, Domestic Violence Flag (if applicable), & Weapon (if available)
-Location : Block-Level Address (e.g., “1200 BLK MAIN ST”), or Street Address, or Geographic Coordinates (latitude and longitude- rounded to three decimal places if necessary)

Please provide the requested data in electronic format, if possible, and notify me in advance of any necessary clarification or related costs exceeding $100.

If certain records or portions of records are exempt from disclosure, please provide a written explanation of the specific exemption(s) and release any non-exempt portions of the requested records.

Thank you for your attention to this request. If you have any questions or require further information, please feel free to contact me. 

Sincerely,
The Data Acquisition Lab

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Data Sharing - LASD
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I’m researching how Los Angeles County law enforcement agencies share CAD, RMS, and JMS data with other agencies. That includes regional systems, national exchanges such as the FBI’s N-DEX and LInX, and private platforms such as SoundThinking’s CrimeTracer and LexisNexis’s Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC, also called the Public Safety Data Exchange or PSDEX).

LASD described its own participation in a 2023 training: “The CrimeTracer Application provides Detectives, Crime Analysts, Investigators and Patrol Personnel with access to Law Enforcement data shared by over 47 agencies within Los Angeles County. Within CrimeTracer, Law Enforcement Personnel also have access to additional Law Enforcement data shared by other agencies outside of Los Angeles County and California.” I am also aware of a related request, reference number 25-4089CO. If records responsive to this request were already produced under that number, please include them here.

I am requesting the following records, from January 1, 2015 through the date of fulfillment:

1) Any contract, addendum, amendment, or terms of service with a private company that governs sharing LASD data with that company or through its platform. This includes agreements with SoundThinking (formerly ShotSpotter) or its predecessor for CrimeTracer, and with LexisNexis Risk Solutions for Accurint or AVCC, including any “AVCC XML Addendum” or Schedule A that specifies which data LASD contributes.
2) Any data sharing agreement, MOU, or other agreement under which LASD shares data in bulk with any public or private data exchange.

If any record is withheld in whole or in part, please follow Government Code §7922.000 and §7922.540. Cite the specific exemption that applies to each record, identify the record by title and page count, and give the name and title of the person responsible for the decision. Under §7922.525, please release all reasonably segregable portions of any record that is partially exempt. If a request item is unclear or too broad, I’m happy to narrow it under §7922.600 and would appreciate a call or email before any denial.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal
